stem: What is the area of the bed, in square feet? ($1$ yard $= 3$ feet)
stimulus: An agricultural research station plants a trial bed of drought-tolerant sorghum. The bed has an area of $6$ square yards.
explanation: A square yard is $3$ feet by $3$ feet, so it holds $3^2 = 9$ square feet. Apply the linear factor twice: $6 \text{ yd}^2 \times \left(\frac{3 \text{ ft}}{1 \text{ yd}}\right)^2 = 6 \times 9 = 54$ square feet.

A.why: You divided $6$ by $3$, which converts in the wrong direction. A foot is smaller than a yard, so the number of square feet has to be larger than $6$, not smaller.

B.why: You multiplied by $3$ only once. That is halfway through the conversion. Area has two dimensions, so you need to apply the factor of $3$ twice.

D.why: You multiplied by $3^3 = 27$, which is the cubic conversion for volume. Area needs the factor squared, not cubed.

stem: What is this speed in feet per second? ($1$ foot $= 12$ inches)
stimulus: A musicology archive digitizes old studio recordings on a reel-to-reel machine. The tape moves past the playback head at $15$ inches per second.
explanation: Only the length unit changes, and "per second" stays the same. $15 \frac{\text{in}}{\text{s}} \times \frac{1 \text{ ft}}{12 \text{ in}} = \frac{15}{12} = 1.25$ feet per second.

A.why: You computed $\frac{12}{15}$ instead of $\frac{15}{12}$. With the fraction upside down, the inches don't cancel.

C.why: You converted both parts of the rate. Changing seconds to minutes as well gives $1.25 \times 60 = 75$ feet per minute. The question asks for feet per second, so "per second" should have stayed as it was.

D.why: You multiplied by $12$ instead of dividing. A foot is longer than an inch, so the tape covers fewer feet than inches each second.

stem: What is the area of the panel, in square inches? ($1$ foot $= 12$ inches)
stimulus: A printmaker carves a large woodcut on a single plywood panel. The panel has an area of $3$ square feet.
explanation: One square foot is $12$ inches by $12$ inches, which is $144$ square inches. Square the linear factor: $3 \text{ ft}^2 \times \left(\frac{12 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ft}}\right)^2 = 3 \times 144 = 432$ square inches.

A.why: You divided $3$ by $12$, which converts in the wrong direction. Inches are smaller than feet, so the area in square inches must be larger than $3$.

B.why: You applied the factor of $12$ only once. For area, you need to multiply by $12$ a second time.

D.why: You multiplied by $12^3 = 1{,}728$, which is the conversion for cubic units. Area uses the factor squared.

stem: What is the volume of the batch, in cubic yards? ($1$ yard $= 3$ feet)
stimulus: A materials science lab mixes a batch of fiber-reinforced concrete to cast test beams. The batch has a volume of $54$ cubic feet, and the supplier prices the mix by the cubic yard.
explanation: A cubic yard is $3$ feet on each edge, so it holds $3^3 = 27$ cubic feet. Apply the linear factor three times: $54 \text{ ft}^3 \times \left(\frac{1 \text{ yd}}{3 \text{ ft}}\right)^3 = \frac{54}{27} = 2$ cubic yards.

B.why: You divided by $3^2 = 9$, which is the conversion for square units. Volume has three dimensions, so you need to divide by $3^3 = 27$.

C.why: You divided by $3$ only once. That is the first of three steps. Volume needs the factor applied three times.

D.why: You multiplied by $27$ instead of dividing. A yard is longer than a foot, so the volume in cubic yards must be smaller than $54$.

stem: What is this speed in meters per hour? ($1$ kilometer $= 1{,}000$ meters)
stimulus: A cartography team maps rural roads with a camera-equipped survey van. While collecting street-level imagery, the van drives at a steady $30$ kilometers per hour.
explanation: Only the distance unit changes, and "per hour" stays the same. $30 \frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} \times \frac{1{,}000 \text{ m}}{1 \text{ km}} = 30{,}000$ meters per hour.

A.why: You divided by $1{,}000$ instead of multiplying. A meter is shorter than a kilometer, so the van covers more meters than kilometers each hour.

B.why: You converted both parts of the rate. Changing hours to minutes as well gives $30{,}000 \div 60 = 500$ meters per minute. The question asks for meters per hour, so the time unit should not change.

C.why: You multiplied by $60$, the number of minutes in an hour, instead of $1{,}000$, the number of meters in a kilometer. Distance is the unit that changes, so you need the length factor.

stem: What is the area of the plate, in square inches? (1 foot = 12 inches)
stimulus: A rectangular copper plate used for etching prints has an area of 3 square feet.
explanation: Area units are squared, so you use the linear factor twice. One square foot is $12 \times 12 = 144$ square inches, so $3 \times 12^2 = 3 \times 144 = 432$ square inches.

A.why: You multiplied by 12 only once, $3 \times 12 = 36$. That turns feet into inches, but square feet need the factor squared.

C.why: You squared the whole product, $(3 \times 12)^2 = 1{,}296$. Only the conversion factor gets squared. The 3 square feet is already an area.

D.why: You cubed the factor, $3 \times 12^3 = 5{,}184$. Cubing is for volume. Area needs the factor squared.

stem: What is the speed of this wave, in kilometers per hour?
stimulus: A seismologist records a primary wave from an earthquake moving through the crust at 6 kilometers per second.
explanation: Only the time unit changes, so you leave the kilometers alone. One hour is $60 \times 60 = 3{,}600$ seconds, so $6 \times 3{,}600 = 21{,}600$ kilometers per hour.

A.why: $6 \times 60 = 360$ is the speed in kilometers per minute. You stopped one conversion short of hours.

B.why: 3,600 is the number of seconds in an hour. That's the conversion factor, and you never multiplied it by the 6 kilometers per second.

D.why: You multiplied by 60 three times, $6 \times 60^3 = 129{,}600$. An hour is $60 \times 60$ seconds. The factor of 60 belongs only twice.

stem: What is the volume of the bin, in cubic centimeters? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)
stimulus: A nutrition lab stores dried lentils for a protein study in a bin with a volume of 0.5 cubic meters.
explanation: Volume units are cubed, so you use the linear factor three times: $0.5 \times 100^3 = 0.5 \times 1{,}000{,}000 = 500{,}000$ cubic centimeters.

A.why: You divided by 100 instead of multiplying. Centimeters are smaller than meters, so the number of cubic centimeters has to be larger.

B.why: You multiplied by 100 only once, $0.5 \times 100 = 50$. A cubic unit needs the factor cubed.

C.why: You squared the factor, $0.5 \times 100^2 = 5{,}000$. That's the rule for area. Volume needs the factor cubed.

stem: What is the area of the plaza, in square feet? (1 yard = 3 feet)
stimulus: A city's urban planning office designs a small public plaza with an area of 50 square yards.
explanation: Area units are squared, so one square yard is $3 \times 3 = 9$ square feet. The plaza is $50 \times 3^2 = 50 \times 9 = 450$ square feet.

A.why: You multiplied by 3 only once, $50 \times 3 = 150$. Square yards need the linear factor squared.

C.why: You cubed the factor, $50 \times 3^3 = 1{,}350$. Cubing is for volume. Area needs the factor squared.

D.why: You squared the factor and then squared it again, $50 \times 9^2 = 4{,}050$. One square yard is 9 square feet, so you multiply by 9 just once.

stem: What is this rate, in milliliters per hour?
stimulus: During an immunology trial, an infusion pump delivers an antibody solution to a patient at a constant rate of 1.5 milliliters per minute.
explanation: Only the time unit changes, so you leave the milliliters alone. There are 60 minutes in an hour, so $1.5 \times 60 = 90$ milliliters per hour.

A.why: You divided by 60 instead of multiplying, $1.5 \div 60 = 0.025$. An hour is longer than a minute, so the pump delivers more in an hour, not less.

B.why: You divided the wrong way, $60 \div 1.5 = 40$. That's the number of minutes the pump takes per 60 milliliters, not a rate in milliliters per hour.

D.why: You treated the rate as per second and multiplied by $3{,}600$. The given rate is per minute, so the factor is only 60.
